findings.evidence: `canonical_human` at lines 53–61 performs only suffix/allowlist checks; the absolute claims occur here at lines 2–6, in `web/Site/Stats.lean` lines 36–43 and 73–77, and in `web/static_files/participation.svg` lines 4, 15, and 17.
findings.fix: Describe the metric as accounts excluding known/conventional automation, or add a mechanism that actually verifies account type; update the module docstring, generated title/note, alt text, caption, and page prose consistently.
findings.issue: The module, generated SVG, and Statistics page call every retained login a human/person and say automation is excluded, although the filter only rejects `[bot]` names and nine known aliases.

findings.evidence: Definitions without following docstrings are at lines 84, 133, 175, 186, 203, and 215; neighboring public functions at lines 53, 64, 115, and 156 are documented.
findings.fix: Add concise object/result docstrings to these functions, or rename implementation-only helpers with a leading underscore.
findings.issue: Public functions `connection_query`, `fetch_connection`, `fetch_all`, `load_data`, `dump_data`, and `render` have no docstrings, leaving their accepted formats, filtering behavior, and return values undocumented.

summary: The documentation overstates bot filtering as verified human participation, and several public script functions lack documentation.
